title: Evaluation of the profinite-point inverse image on a contractible affine
statement: Use the universes of [def-weil-size-convention] and the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let $p_X^*=\pi_X^{-1}a^*$ be the geometric inverse image from sheaves on profinite sets defined in [lem-weil-pbc-profinite-point-pullback]. Let $F$ be a sheaf of sets, abelian groups, or commutative rings on profinite sets with finite jointly surjective coverings. Let $U$ be an affine object of $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ which is weakly contractible, meaning evaluation at $U$ sends epimorphisms of sheaves of sets to surjections. The quotient space $\pi_0(|U|)$ of connected components is profinite, and there is a canonical identification $(p_X^*F)(U)\cong F(\pi_0(|U|))$, natural in $F$ and in morphisms between such $U$. The identification preserves addition and multiplication when present. The topology on $\pi_0(|U|)$ is the quotient topology: a subset is open if and only if its inverse image in $|U|$ is open.

For coefficient naturality, use the map induced by the left Kan extension functor; compatibility with the unit is its lanUnit naturality. Specialize simultaneous Kan naturality to the identity of U; the induced component map is the identity, checked on representatives of ConnectedComponents. Cancel the invertible sheafification unit and use its naturality. For naturality in a:V to U, specialize the coefficient morphism to the identity and apply the same cancellation with the restriction-naturality equation of the unit. This constructs PointBasisEvaluationProperty for the relative sheafified Kan extension in any coefficient category with the required colimits and sheafification.

Compose the two sheafPullbackConstruction adjunctions for the former; use the relative adjunction for the latter. Their right adjoints agree definitionally. Mathlib Adjunction.leftAdjointUniq gives a natural isomorphism between the left adjoints. Compose its evaluated components with the preceding comparisons; naturality of this isomorphism proves both equations after transport. Specialize to sets, abelian groups and commutative rings. The algebraic comparisons are isomorphisms in their coefficient categories, so preserve operations.
